item.text:
**8B.7**

**Assessment**
Partly yes, but uneven. The strongest 2024 movement was in macro stabilization: inflation fell, reserves rose, growth recovered, and policy credibility improved. But the gains were incomplete and did not yet translate into broad poverty reduction or strong structural change. On political and institutional outcomes, the direction was often negative: repression, media control, and judicial weakening worsened.

**Accepted claims**

- **Macro stabilization improved materially** | *IMF* | **2024-09-27** | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr | The IMF said growth returned, inflation fell to single digits, reserves doubled over the prior year, and external pressures eased. This is the clearest evidence that outcomes moved in the direction of Sharif’s stabilization agenda. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`, `8B.2`
- **Inflation crossed into single digits** | *Reuters via Investing.com* | **2024-09-02** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/pakistan-annual-inflation-slows-to-96-first-singledigit-stat-in-nearly-3-years-3596921 | Reuters reported annual inflation slowed to 9.6% in August 2024, the first single-digit reading in nearly three years. That is a direct outcome move in the direction of stabilization. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`
- **Stability remained visible by year-end** | *World Bank* | **2024-10-10** | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank | The World Bank said FY24 growth recovered to 2.5% and macro conditions improved, helped by lower inflation and prudent policy. This supports a qualified positive reading, though the Bank also stressed the recovery was not yet broad-based. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`
- **Earlier-year baseline was still very weak** | *World Bank* | **2024-04-02** | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p | The Bank said growth was expected to be only 1.8% and poverty was still around 40% early in 2024, with reserves and import constraints still binding. This is important context: 2024 started from a very weak inherited position, so any gains had to clear a high hurdle. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.2`

- **Poverty did not improve** | *World Bank* | **2024-10-10** | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank | The World Bank said poverty still increased, reaching 40.5% by FY24. That cuts directly against any claim that outcome indicators had broadly moved in the welfare direction Sharif said he wanted. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.2`, `8B.3`
- **Structural reform remained incomplete** | *IMF* | **2024-10-10** | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152 | The IMF still described weak governance, a narrow tax base, very low investment, and insufficient health and education spending. That means the deeper outcomes Sharif’s program implied were not yet materializing. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`
- **Utility relief helped, but only partially** | *Reuters via Investing.com* | **2024-09-07** | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192 | The government renegotiated expensive power contracts because energy prices were hurting households and firms. This is a real output-side adjustment, but it also shows the pressure remained severe and relief was only partial. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.6`, `8B.3`

- **Rights and civic outcomes worsened** | *Human Rights Watch* | **2024-10-09** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent | HRW reported over 500 arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile internet cuts against peaceful protesters. That is a negative outcome on political freedom and public order, not evidence of successful, legitimate state improvement. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`
- **Minority protection did not improve** | *Amnesty International* | **2024-06-21** | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ | Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked Ahmadi rites, with authorities failing to ensure safety. That is direct counterevidence to any claim that vulnerable-group outcomes moved in the claimed direction. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.3`
- **Information access worsened** | *Reuters via Investing.com* | **2024-04-17** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | The state confirmed blocking X around the election period on national-security grounds. That is an observable negative outcome for scrutiny and public access, even if it did not stop macro stabilization. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`
- **Judicial independence weakened** | *The Guardian* | **2024-10-21** | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps | Critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid intimidation allegations. That points to institutional outcomes moving away from the ruler’s implied claim of orderly governance. | IDs: `8B.7`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`

**Search gap**
- The strongest measurable progress in 2024 was macroeconomic, not distributive or institutional.
- I found no solid 2024 evidence that poverty, rights protection, media freedom, or judicial independence improved in line with Sharif’s stated or revealed goals.
- Some positive macro trends were real but still lagged, partial, and vulnerable to external constraints, so the cleanest reading is “macro yes, broad outcomes no.”
